title: DayRecall — AI memory for your whole day | Apple Watch & iPhone
description: DayRecall listens on Apple Watch or iPhone during the hours you choose, turns what was said into text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day.

app_description: An AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone. During the hours you choose it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day with the exact words.
app_features: Listens all day on Apple Watch, with no iPhone nearby; works with iPhone alone too
Speech becomes text on the iPhone and the audio is deleted
Ask about your day and get the exact words, with the moment they were said
Marks who said what: Me, Other 1, Other 2
Follows conversations in up to three languages, translated into yours
Picks out to-dos, deadlines and meetings for you to confirm
No account and no server; answers use Apple’s on-device model

how_02: One tap in the morning. Answers all day.
how_03: A strip of sound is scanned: only the bursts of speech light up and are kept; the quiet in between is skipped.
how_05: Your Apple Watch listens during the hours you choose, even with your iPhone left behind. One tap in the morning, and it stops on its own. Our in-house ultra-light speech model runs right on the watch and keeps only the moments when someone is talking.

how_08: Your iPhone turns the speech into text on the device, deletes the audio, and picks out the to-dos, deadlines and meetings. It can also tell what you said from what others said.
how_09: Memories slide into the iPhone and it locks; anything heading for the cloud is stopped and comes back.
how_11: Your memories stay on your iPhone, and answers use Apple’s on-device model. You can choose your own cloud API later; nothing is sent until you allow it.
devices_02: Your watch doesn’t need your phone nearby.
devices_03: Apple Watch listens on its own, all day. Recordings wait on the watch and go to your iPhone every two hours, and if your iPhone isn’t around, they catch up as soon as the two reconnect, say when you get home in the evening. Your iPhone never has to stay connected.

battery_02: Listens all day. Barely touches the battery.
battery_03: A workday from 9:00 to 18:00: the conversations light up along the day, and the battery that listening uses grows to only about 8%.
battery_04: A professional-grade, ultra-light speech model built in-house: just 2,561 parameters, running on our own accelerated inference kernels and making a call every tenth of a second, right on the watch.
battery_05: Only speech is kept. Silence, keyboards and fans are filtered out before they cost any battery. Everything from the architecture to the kernels was designed for the watch, drawing on our doctoral research in AI acceleration.

features_06: What did Sam promise? When is the report due? Every answer shows where it came from, down to the line that was said.
features_08: See a day as a timeline, flip back through past days, and search everything you’ve heard.

privacy_02: Text only. On your iPhone. Your call.

faq.a: DayRecall is an AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone, made for people who forget things. During the hours you choose, it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day with the exact words and where they came from.

faq.q: Do I need an Apple Watch?
faq.a: No. DayRecall works best with Apple Watch, and your iPhone can also listen on its own. When both listen, your day is one timeline, and what both heard is shown once.

faq.q: Does my iPhone have to stay near my watch?
faq.a: No. Your Apple Watch keeps its recordings and sends them to your iPhone every two hours, or as soon as the two reconnect, for example when you get home in the evening.
No. Speech is turned into text on your iPhone, and then the audio is deleted. Only the text is kept.

faq.q: Where is my data, and who can see it?
faq.a: On your iPhone. There is no account and no DayRecall server. Answers use Apple’s on-device model, and nothing leaves your iPhone unless you choose to use your own cloud API or hand a day to an AI app.

faq.q: How much battery does it use?
faq.a: Very little. Our in-house ultra-light speech model keeps only the moments when someone is talking. In internal testing on Apple Watch Series 11, listening added about 0.9% battery per hour.
The app comes in 13 languages. It can also transcribe a conversation that switches between up to three languages, and translate the other languages into yours.
DayRecall is in beta and coming soon to the App Store.
